text:
sam: Quick heads-up — noticed a reproducible perf dip on the multi-variant routing experiment we rolled yesterday. throughput down ~18% on purple-cluster when a small compat-set triggers fallback to older variants.

mia: ugh. observable where? traces or perf counters?

sam: p50 went 40ms -> 65ms, p95 190ms -> 410ms. KV cache hit-rate drops from ~79% to ~61% when fallback starts coalescing mixed-variant batches. Logs attached in thread.

raj: is this the sticky-routing canary or the fast-fallthrough policy?

sam: fast-fallthrough. routing policy picks a lower-cost variant but compat-merge logic ends up combining requests with different kernel profiles. kernel selector then falls back to generic path for the whole batch.

alex: that matches my local repro — if batch has mixed tensor shapes / quantization flags, kernel chooser picks a safe kernel (slower). We also saw KV eviction pressure.

sam: pasted a short profile snippet:```
job=multi-variant-canary
batch_cnt=1200
avg_batch_size=5.9
kv_hit_rate=0.78 -> 0.62 (after fallback spike)
kernel_selected: cutlass_fastfp16 (baseline) -> generic_gemm_fallback
p50=42ms -> 68ms
p95=210ms -> 480ms
cpu_util=34% gpu_util=78%
```

mia: thanks. two immediate lines to check: 1) batch formation policy (min_merge_window / merge_compat_threshold) 2) token_budget enforcement — we might be forcing bigger batches that straddle variant boundaries.

raj: adding numbers from queue-trace: `merge_compat_threshold=0.65`, `min_batch_age_ms=6`, `token_budget_per_batch=1200`. With mixed variants token_budget is reached sooner due to longer kernel latencies leading to stray short-lived batches.

alex: hypothesis: when routing mixes variants, the runtime's continuous-batcher should bias toward compat-preserving merges even if it means smaller immediate throughput. So tweak: increase `compat_pref_weight` in scheduler + lower `token_budget_per_batch` for multi-variant routes.

sam: tried quick tweak on canary: `compat_pref_weight=1.8` and `token_budget_per_batch=900`. Results: avg_batch_size dropped 5.9 -> 4.7 but kv_hit_rate recovered to 74% and p95 back to ~230ms. throughput slightly down but tail latency much better.

perf-bot: perf/regression check queued: compare jobs 1998887000..1998887800. ETA 12m.

mia: nice. do we have kernel selection traces to prove the fallback is the primary cause vs kv-thrashing?

sam: yes — pulled kernel timeline per batch. When mixed-variant batch enters, first kernel decision sets generic path; subsequent requests in same batch don't re-evaluate so whole batch pays. KV thrash is secondary: generic kernel increases inference time -> more concurrent batches -> higher KV timeouts and evictions.

raj: sounds like two mitigation axes: 1) routing-level: avoid mixing variants in same queue (soft-affinity / sticky-compat buckets) 2) runtime-level: allow per-request kernel hints within a batch (risky) or faster fallback kernels.

alex: runtime change pros/cons: per-request kernel hints would require splitting kernel-launchs within a batch => reduces batching benefits. Faster fallback kernels need engineering but preserve batch aggregation.

mia: short-term: prefer routing policy change + batching heuristics. set `merge_compat_threshold=0.8` for multi-variant routes and make token budget adaptive: `token_budget_per_batch = base_budget * compat_factor` where compat_factor < 1 when variant-mix > 0.2.

sam: implemented canary config: `merge_compat_threshold=0.82`, `adaptive_token_budget: enabled`, `compat_factor_cutoff=0.2`, `compat_pref_weight=1.8`. Observed: kv_hit_rate 76%, p95 260ms, throughput -6% vs baseline but much less tail variance.

perf-bot: regression check finished: no severe regressions. p50 within -4%, p95 improved vs previous canary (not production baseline). Full report: https://perf/reports/1998887776 (internal).

alex: next actions: 1) run longer 3h canary to watch KV steady-state 2) run a perf sweep where we simulate 30% variant-mix at different `min_batch_age_ms` (2,6,12) and `token_budget` (700..1400) 3) consider a runtime micro-optimization to detect first-kernel mismatch earlier and split batch only when beneficial.

sam: +1. I'll update the canary config and schedule the 3h run. putting a short RFC in eng-runtime channel tomorrow with numbers and recommended default heuristics.

mia: cheers. if perf sweep shows consistent tail wins, we should change default compat threshold for multi-variant routes.

raj: also adding a windshield test for KV hotset eviction under mixed-variant noise. if eviction rate > 10% we need to throttle burst merges.

sam: thanks all. ping me if you want the raw traces. planning to roll routing change to 25% traffic after 3h canary if stable. :thumbsup:
